title: Digital Manufacturing
description: Introduction to manufacturing with two-dimensional and three-dimensional digital layout input. Creating designs using standard Two-Dimensional (2D) and Three-Dimensional (3D) design software, e.g. AutoCAD and SolidWorks, and 3D scanner. Optimization of project design for construction on 3D printers. Examination of materials available for 3D printing.
outcomes: Evaluate print quality and determine print parameter optimizations that may improve quality for 2D and 3D manufacturing equipment
Demonstrate proper alignment and operating procedures for safe and effective operation of the 3D printer
objectives: Identify common 3D file formats, and the sequence of file processing used to create a 3D file for printing
Evaluate a 3D design and determine the parameters for optimum construction with 3D printing
Design project using 2D/3D software, e.g. AutoCAD and SolidWorks
content: 2D and 3D manufacturing equipment and printer safety, setup, and operating procedures
Equipment: 3D Scanner, 3D printer and Laser Cutter
Equipment Setup, Operating Procedures and Safety
3D design file formats: Stereolithography (.STL) , Wavefront 3D Object File (.OBJ), AutoCAD FBX (.FBX), COLLADA (.DAE)
Dimensional accuracy and stability and impact of nozzle and bed temperatures on work piece stability
lab: Discuss 2D/3D printer safety and operating procedures
Process 2D/3D project file for optimum 2D/3D printing
assignments: Students are expected to work on homework in order to learn the materials
Example: Work on 3D design using 3D software.
Students use the concepts and technical skills learned in the class to analyze and solve practical problems.
Example: Troubleshoot 3D printing issue and 3D printer issue.
Students demonstrate their understanding of the materials by designing a 3D object.
Example: Create 3D project designs and produce the projects on the 3D printer.
